title: Investigatio motuum, quibus laminae et virgae elasticae contremiscunt

deep.reconstruction:
§30 treats Case III: an elastic rod (Euler–Bernoulli beam) that is free at end E (s=0) and clamped ('quasi muro infixa') at end F (s=a). Euler seeks all its 'regular' vibrations, i.e. normal modes. From earlier sections the separated mode shape is y(s) = α e^{s/f} + β e^{-s/f} + γ sin(s/f) + δ cos(s/f), with time factor sin(ζ + t√(2g/k)).

The free-end conditions at s=0 are y''=0 and y'''=0. They give α+β−δ=0 and α−β−γ=0, hence γ=α−β and δ=α+β, 'as before'.

The clamped-end conditions at s=a, with ω=a/f, are y=0 and y'=0:
(1) α e^ω + β e^{-ω} + γ sin ω + δ cos ω = 0,
(2) α e^ω − β e^{-ω} + γ cos ω − δ sin ω = 0.
Substituting γ and δ gives
α(e^ω + sin ω + cos ω) + β(e^{-ω} − sin ω + cos ω) = 0,
α(e^ω + cos ω − sin ω) − β(e^{-ω} + cos ω + sin ω) = 0.
Each equation yields α/β. With p = sin ω + cos ω and q = sin ω − cos ω, the two expressions are (−e^{-ω}+q)/(e^ω+p) and (e^{-ω}+p)/(e^ω−q). Equating them is the vanishing of the 2×2 determinant.

The next page cross-multiplies to 2 + (p−q)(e^ω+e^{-ω}) + p²+q² = 0. Since p²+q²=2 and p−q=2cos ω, this becomes cos ω = −2/(e^ω+e^{-ω}), i.e. cos ω cosh ω = −1. This is the classical cantilever frequency equation, with first root ω≈1.875. The frequencies are proportional to ω² c√(2gb)/a².
errors: No mathematical error on this page; every substitution and both expressions for α/β check out.
Typographical slip in the print: 'sin ω − cos ω = g', where q is meant; the next formula uses q.
The title reads 'alter terminos liber'; 'terminus' is meant.

ideas.what: Separated (normal-mode) solution of the fourth-order beam equation as a combination of exponentials and trigonometric functions (cosh/sinh/sin/cos form).
ideas.where_published: E65 (Methodus inveniendi, 1744, Additamentum I De curvis elasticis); E526 itself

ideas.what: Boundary conditions for a free end (y''=y'''=0) and a clamped end (y=y'=0).
ideas.modern_name: Free and clamped beam boundary conditions

ideas.what: Determinant condition reducing to the frequency equation cos ω cosh ω = −1 for the cantilever (completed on the next page).
ideas.where_published: E65 Additamentum I; D. Bernoulli, Comm. Acad. Petrop. 13 (1741–43)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful re-derivation of the well-known cantilever frequency equation, already given by D. Bernoulli and Euler in the 1740s and discussed in Truesdell's history of elastic vibrations. Nothing on the page is new.
transcription_corrections: 'fin. ω − cof. ω = g' is printed as g but must be read as q.
'ſin.'/'coſ.' are rendered as 'fin.'/'cof.' in the transcription; they denote sine and cosine.
The title's 'terminos' is a printing error for 'terminus'.
